newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian PM says "power ministers" to keep jobs.
newsitem.headline: Russian PM says "power ministers" to keep jobs.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Friday the interior and defence ministers and the head of the Federal Security Service would not be affected by a cabinet reshuffle now under way.

"There will be no personnel changes in any power structures now," he told the State Duma lower house of parliament. President Boris Yeltsin launched a dramatic cabinet reshuffle on Monday which is expected to be completed early next week.
The heads of the interior and defence ministries and the Federal Service are collectively known as the "power ministers" responsible for maintaining national security.
Like the foreign minister, they report directly to Yeltsin, bypassing the prime minister.
Defence Minister Igor Rodionov has been publicly at odds with members of Yeltsin's entourage and had recently been rumoured to be facing the axe in the reshuffle.
Chernomyrdin told the Duma that further nominations would be made early next week to fill new posts established by the government shake-up but he added there would be no more sackings.
Yeltsin, worried by growing public discontent over a protracted economic downturn, has put pro-market liberals in broad control of economic policy.
Chernomyrdin has said the new cabinet's top priorities will be speeding up reforms and acting to end big delays in payment of wages and pensions.
Chernomyrdin said earlier that the government changes would be completed after Yeltsin returns on Saturday from Helsinki, where he has been holding talks with U.S. President Bill Clinton.
